chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Umm Sa'id al-Ahmasiyyah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you mention regarding the virtue of visiting the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He replied, 'O Umm Sa'id! It is mentioned that its reward is equal to that of a Hajj and an 'Umrah, and there is this much reward in it.' And he spread his two hands [or his hand] and bent his fingers.

key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation (to the graves of Imams or prophets)
key_terms.قَبْر الْحُسَيْن: The grave of Husayn ibn Ali

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) to emphasize the preeminent status of Karbala as a spiritual sanctuary, equating the visitation of Imam Husayn’s grave with the combined merit of Hajj and 'Umrah. The Imam’s gesture of spreading his hands and inclining his fingers serves as a physical metaphor for the vastness of this reward, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition that views Ziyarah not merely as a ritual but as a means of connecting with the divine presence through the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, and from Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdil Ḥamīd, from Yūnus ibn Ya’qūb, from Um Sa’īd Al-Aḥmasiyyah, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), “What do you say is the reward for the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.)?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “O Um Sa’īd! We say that it is equal to the reward of a Hajj and an ‘Umrah, and there is this much reward in it.” Um Sa’īd added that the Imam (a.s.) stretched open his arms with his fingers bent.
